title: LEGOLAND Windsor Tips: How to Save and Plan Your Day
description: LEGOLAND Windsor tips for families: the best ages, height checks, saving with the Merlin pass and rail offers, quieter days and how to plan your route.
h1: LEGOLAND Windsor tips: plan your day and save
intro: LEGOLAND Windsor is built for families with younger children, and it’s one of the UK’s most popular days out. Here’s how to plan a brilliant, better-value visit.

image.alt: A close-up of colourful toy building bricks

cardText: Best ages, height checks, quieter days and real ways to save.

blocks.title: Scout’s LEGOLAND route
blocks.text: Most families stop at the first rides they see. Head to the far side of the park first and work back towards the entrance as the day goes on.
points: Measure your kids before you go: height limits decide everything
Bring a change of clothes for the water rides

sections.html: LEGOLAND is designed for families with children aged roughly 2 to 12. Many rides are gentle, and lots let younger children ride with an adult. Older teens may prefer thrill parks.

• Book online, ahead: date-based pricing rewards quieter days and early booking.
  • Merlin Annual Pass: LEGOLAND Windsor is included. See if a pass pays off.
  • Rail offers: in 2026 the Days Out Guide listed a rail-ticket discount here. Check the live listing.
  • Bring a picnic: food inside theme parks adds up quickly.

• Arrive before opening and head deeper into the park first.
  • See MINILAND in the busy middle of the day. It doesn’t need queuing.
  • Use the app for live queue times.
  • Ask about the Ride Access Pass in advance if anyone in your group needs it. See our queue tips.

faqs.q: What age is LEGOLAND Windsor best for?
faqs.a: It’s designed for families with children aged roughly 2 to 12. Many rides suit younger children riding with an adult.

faqs.q: Is LEGOLAND Windsor included in the Merlin Annual Pass?
faqs.a: Yes. LEGOLAND Windsor Resort is included in Merlin Annual Passes, subject to each pass’s exclusion dates and pre-booking.
